themes_detail.label: Street Lights Going Dark
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints spiked to 23 THIS WEEK, up 292% from the 5.9-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.4), signaling a sudden infrastructure failure affecting public safety and nighttime visibility in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 23 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs 5.9 weekly average (292% spike, z-score 7.4)
Spike emerged suddenly this week with no prior warning in the 8-week baseline
Community board has repeatedly requested transit/DOT infrastructure funding, suggesting ongoing neglect
reporting_angles: Contact DOT to understand cause of simultaneous failures across district—equipment failure, contractor delay, or budget issue?
Interview residents about safety concerns during evening hours; check for crime reports during outages
Verify if this correlates with other infrastructure complaints (SPIT, ERT spikes) suggesting systemic maintenance breakdown

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints hit 10 THIS WEEK, a 900% spike from the 1.0-per-week baseline (z-score: 8.05), indicating either a sudden proliferation of illegal vending or a concentrated enforcement push targeting street commerce.
evidence: 10 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.0 weekly average (900% spike, z-score 8.05)
Spike is brand new—emerged this week with no gradual trend
Could reflect either illegal vending outbreak or NYPD/DOC enforcement blitz
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and local business owners about enforcement intensity and any recent policy changes
Check with Community Board 9 and NYC Department of Consumer Affairs—was there a coordinated enforcement action?
Assess impact on informal economy; are vendors from low-income communities being disproportionately targeted?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Resurgence
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK, up 433% from the 1.1-per-week baseline (z-score: 6.24), representing a fresh outbreak of vandalism in a historically managed district.
evidence: 6 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs 1.1 weekly average (433% spike, z-score 6.24)
Spike represents a sudden outbreak, not a gradual trend
Concentrated in a district with university presence (Columbia) and high foot traffic
reporting_angles: Map graffiti complaints geographically—are they clustered near transit hubs, parks, or residential blocks?
Interview Parks Dept or Sanitation about removal timelines and whether vandalism is organized or opportunistic
Speak with Columbia University and local residents about quality-of-life impacts and visibility

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints surged to 94 THREE WEEKS AGO, up 243% from the 27.4-per-week baseline (z-score: 5.92), suggesting a cluster of loud business operations or construction impacting residential areas.
evidence: 94 commercial noise complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs 27.4 weekly average (243% spike, z-score 5.92)
Spike is 3 weeks old, suggesting potential sustained issue if still present
Residential noise complaints also chronically high (1,468 over 90 days), indicating noise is neighborhood-wide concern
reporting_angles: Identify which commercial operations generated the spike—new venues, expanded hours, construction, or deliveries?
Check if spike has subsided or persists; if ongoing, investigate enforcement response
Interview residents and small business owners about noise ordinance compliance and enforcement gaps

themes_detail.label: Building Maintenance Crisis Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Four separate 311 categories—SPIT (1020% spike), OUTSIDE BUILDING (586% spike), ELEVATOR (300% spike), and ERT (1100% spike)—all spiked 2-3 weeks ago, suggesting a systemic building maintenance failure across the district affecting structural integrity and resident safety.
evidence: SPIT spike: 7 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs 0.6 avg (1020%, z-score 9.16)
ERT spike: 3 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs 0.2 avg (1100%, z-score 6.35)
OUTSIDE BUILDING spike: 6 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs 0.9 avg (586%, z-score 6.57)
ELEVATOR spike: 7 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs 1.8 avg (300%, z-score 5.42)
Convergence of multiple building-safety categories suggests either external event (weather, grid failure) or landlord non-compliance wave
reporting_angles: Investigate what triggered the multi-category spike 3 weeks ago—storm damage, DOB crackdown, or landlord financing crisis?
Request DOB inspection data for the district over the same timeframe; cross-check violations with 311 complaints
Interview tenant advocates and legal services about eviction/neglect patterns; profile buildings with repeated violations
Assess whether this correlates with 364 DOB permits filed (many alterations)—are landlords cutting corners?
